title: TF module upgrade sanity scenarios and smoke checklist
content:
Purpose / scope:
This doc captures sanity scenarios, lightweight smoke tests, and known terraform module gotchas to run when upgrading private-deploy TF modules or performing coordinated runtime upgrades in VPC/on-prem installs. The goal is quick detection of the top 80% failure modes during a rolling upgrade so SRE/SEs can abort early and collect targeted debugging artifacts.

Context and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments (VPC or on-prem) using the terraform modules in infra/terraform-modules (module versioning matters).
- Assumes remote state in S3/GCS with state locking enabled, and that operator has access to the environment workspace.
- Works for planned minor/patch upgrades of modules (e.g., module v1.x -> v1.y). For major upgrades (breaking TF/schema changes), follow full upgrade runbook.

Quick preflight (fast, run before terraform plan/apply):
- confirm git branch + PR linked: GH PR exists and reviewers set.
- git sha, module version in PR description and change log.
- terraform fmt & validate: terraform fmt -check && terraform validate
- backend init: terraform init -backend-config=... and confirm state lock acquires
- workspace check: terraform workspace show -> expected workspace
- provider pin check: verify provider versions pinned (aws, google, kubernetes)
- state refresh: terraform plan -refresh-only -> zero unexpected changes
- quick smoke permissions: attempt dry-run API calls for cloud creds (e.g., aws sts get-caller-identity, gcloud auth list)

TF plan sanity checks (on plan output):
- planned changes count reasonable (e.g., expected number of nodes, not entire cluster).
- no resource replacement of long-lived infra (e.g., no replacement of load balancer subnets or KMS keys unless intended).
- check for tainted or unknown resources: grep for "Force replacement"
- ensure depends_on ordering didn't disappear for critical resources like vpn/gateway or k8s provider bootstrap

Minimal smoke apply (canary / low-risk path):
- target apply small scope: terraform apply -target=module.runtime[0] (or similar) to upgrade single canary pool
- verify state updates and statefile size not unexpectedly large
- check for provider timeouts or rate limits in apply logs

Post-apply runtime quick checks (first 10 minutes):
- verify system-level: check kernel/gpu drivers on nodes (nvidia-smi, lsmod | grep nvidia)
- container runtime healthy: sudo systemctl status containerd or docker; docker ps | grep redwood-runtime
- k8s health (if using k8s): kubectl get nodes && kubectl get pods -A | grep CrashLoopBackOff
- logs: journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 || docker logs <runtime-container> --tail 200
- network connectivity: curl -sS https://metadata.redwood.local/health || check LB health endpoints
- KV cache / model mount: check /mnt/models presence and read permissions, run quick model-load smoke (curl to local health probe that loads small model shard)

Key smoke assertions (must pass within timeout):
- API ping (TLS handshake + auth): curl -k -I https://<edge-ip>/v1/health -> 200/401 expected variants
- Inference dry-run: call a cheap route (generate 1 token) against upgraded instance and assert response latency under threshold
- KV cache warmup: repeated inference hit should show cache hits in metrics (console or /metrics endpoint)
- Metrics and logs: metrics endpoint responds, forwarding to observability backend works (check last ingestion timestamp)

Terraform module-specific notes & known quirks (collected from past incidents):
- state drift in module.network: MTU mismatches cause packet drops post-upgrade (check ip link show dev <if> mtu).
- provider version bumps can reorder resource replacement (pin providers during upgrade cycle).
- implicit dependency on DNS records: some modules assumed DNS propagation; add explicit depends_on for critical LB->DNS records to avoid transient 404s.
- module outputs changed shape: intermediate scripts that parse state may break; add backward-compatible outputs or update scripts in same PR.
- remote-exec/userdata ordering: onprem AMI userdata that installs drivers sometimes races with cloud-init; add sleep/retry loops in bootstrap scripts and idempotent checks.

Common failure patterns & action checklist (fast triage):
1) Nodes stuck in provisioning or NotReady
- check cloud provider console / onprem BMC power state
- check kubelet logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200
- check certificate expiry: ls /var/lib/kubelet/pki/*
- quick fix: restart kubelet/systemd unit, or reboot node if kernel modules not loaded

2) Container runtime failures after upgrade
- symptoms: containerd/dockerd crashes or OOM for runtimeshim
- check: systemctl status container runtime, journalctl -u containerd -n 200, dmesg for OOM killer
- workaround: increase containerd restart limit temporarily, rollout smaller canary, or revert to previous container image tag

3) TF apply hangs / deadlocks on remote state lock
- check lock owner: terraform state pull or check S3/GCS lock file; ask colleague if they have an active apply
- forced unlock only after coordination (terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>)

4) KMS/certs failures (Secrets fail to decrypt)
- symptoms: pods fail with 403 or missing secret errors
- checks: verify KMS key policy, KMS IAM roles, test encrypt/decrypt with operator creds
- recovery: rotate temporary encryption key or restore secrets from backups; ensure operator has kms:Decrypt rights

5) Network partition / MTU / firewall rules cause timeouts
- symptoms: services healthy locally but unable to reach external model storage
- checks: iptables -L -n -v; tc qdisc show dev <if>; MTU mismatch test: ping -M do -s 1472 <peer>

Upgrade gating criteria (stop and roll back if any fail):
- >5% increase in 5m error rate vs baseline for critical route
- any sustained CrashLoopBackOff on core infra pods after 10 minutes
- inability to decrypt customer-managed keys or massive auth failures
- infrastructure replacement larger than expected (e.g., whole LB or KMS replacement)

Fallback & rollback notes (fast revert):
- maintain previous module versions in a stable branch (stable/<env>) that can be re-applied quickly
- snapshot cluster state where possible (etcd snapshot, K8s manifests export)
- terraform rollback pattern: checkout stable branch -> terraform init -> terraform apply -auto-approve (do not try to mix new and old state in same plan)
- if resource replacement happened unexpectedly, escalate to infra leads and consider manual resource reconciliation rather than automated rollback

Artifacts to collect when filing incident ticket (PD-xxx):
- terraform plan output and terraform apply logs (raw)
- terraform state list for impacted modules
- system logs: journalctl -u <units> and docker/containerd logs (last 500 lines)
- k8s: poddescribe + pod logs for impacted pods, events (kubectl describe pod; kubectl get events -A)
- network captures if needed (tcpdump -i <if> -w /tmp/capture.pcap)
- timestamps and git sha of applied changes

Short checklist for field engineers (copy/paste):
- [ ] confirm PR + module version and remote state backend
- [ ] terraform fmt && terraform init && terraform validate
- [ ] run terraform plan and sanity review (search for "replacement")
- [ ] apply to single canary target; verify node/container runtimes
- [ ] run inference dry-run and metrics smoke -> verify latency and cache behavior
- [ ] check KMS and secrets decryption path
- [ ] collect logs and attach to JIRA if anything abnormal

Notes / open questions / follow-ups:
- Automate the model-load smoke endpoint to be part of TF post-apply tests (GH issue created).
- Investigate adding MTU and iptables preflight checks into terraform null_resource to catch common onprem issues earlier.
- Add a small TF module test harness that can run in CI to exercise provider upgrades (PR: GH:infra/tests#79).

History / incident references (for context):
- PD-432: MTU mismatch after network module upgrade -> caused degraded grpc streams to model storage
- PD-512: provider bump replaced LB -> required manual DNS reconciliation
- PD-601: KMS policy change rolled out without service account update -> secrets inaccessible until revert

If you're running this and hit something not covered, ping #private-deployments with the collected artifacts above and tag @Maya_Rivera or @Lucas_Chen for triage.
